# Guided AI GRC Build

**Proposal for Tamarack Instruments**
**Prepared for Dana Whitfield, General Counsel**

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands, operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States and has about 1,100 staff. Its AI maturity is at the piloting stage. Its three AI use cases are at different stages:

* **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
* **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
* **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. ISO/IEC 42001 is a certification target. Work toward it is to start next year, and the start date is not fixed. In June 2026 an internal audit finding recorded no inventory of AI systems.

Dana Whitfield has stated the objective: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

Three constraints shape the build:

* Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
* Customer data must stay in the EU.
* The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

The program fee of US$60,000 sits within the approved budget figure. Whether the program falls within the current fiscal year is a question to confirm at intake.

## 2. The Case for a Guided Build

A conventional consulting engagement delivers a governance system that the Client receives but did not build. The Guided AI GRC Build reverses this. Over twelve weeks the Client's own build team constructs each artifact between sessions, using open frameworks and supported by one live virtual workshop and one coaching session each week. The team will be drawn from these roles:

* General Counsel
* CISO
* Head of Quality
* Head of Data
* German plant manager
* Two internal auditors

At Week 12 the people who will run the Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS) are the people who designed it. They understand why each control exists, can explain it to an auditor and can adapt it when visual inspection and sales forecasting change the risk picture. ISO/IEC 42001 work next year would then start from an operating system rather than a document set.

The program draws on two open frameworks:

* GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) for the governance, risk and compliance structure.
* Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) for governed workflows and human oversight.

Three principles run throughout: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human.

Including two internal auditors in the build team strengthens evidence design. It also raises an independence question. We propose that the internal auditors shape evidence requirements and lead the Week 12 readiness review, without owning operating controls. How the internal audit function prefers to preserve its independence is a question to confirm at intake.

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

| Week | Spine focus | Tailoring to Tamarack Instruments | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mobilization, charter and roles | Charter scope covers all three use cases. Roles are assigned across the build team. A works council consultation checkpoint is designed into the plan (confirm with external counsel). | Context of the organization, leadership and roles |
| 2 | AI system inventory | Entry order: the chatbot first, as the deployed system interacting with customers. The visual inspection pilot second, as the system tied to the Q2 2027 objective. Sales forecasting third, as a planned entry. Any further AI systems identified are then added. The inventory responds directly to the June 2026 internal audit finding. | AIMS scope and AI system records |
| 3 | Classification and risk methodology | All three use cases are classified against EU AI Act categories and GDPR relevance. Classification outcomes: confirm with external counsel. | Planning and AI risk criteria |
| 4 | Risk and impact assessments | Full assessments for the chatbot and visual inspection, and a scoping assessment for sales forecasting. Impacts on production staff feed the works council checkpoint. | AI risk assessment and AI system impact assessment |
| 5 | Risk register and treatment | An operating register is built, with treatments that include the EU customer data constraint wherever the inventory shows it applies. | AI risk treatment |
| 6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | The core policy set is drafted for adoption. Policy wording with legal effect: confirm with external counsel. | AI policy and leadership commitment |
| 7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Lifecycle gates are defined for the visual inspection move from pilot to production, along with an intake route for sales forecasting. | Operational planning and AI system life cycle |
| 8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection begins | Suppliers for each system are identified from the inventory (currently `Unknown`). Data location terms are checked against the EU constraint. Contract terms: confirm with external counsel. | Third-party relationships and documented information |
| 9 | Governed workflows and human oversight (Slow AI Kitchen) | The chatbot is the first candidate governed workflow. Human oversight of inspection decisions is designed. The second workflow is decided as set out below. | Use of AI systems and human oversight |
| 10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Monitoring is set up for chatbot response quality and inspection performance. | Monitoring, measurement and evaluation |
| 11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | Incident and change routes are built, followed by the first structured evidence review. | Nonconformity, corrective action and improvement |
| 12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | The internal auditors lead the readiness walkthrough, which produces a gap view for next year's ISO/IEC 42001 work. | Internal audit and management review readiness |

**ISO/IEC 42001 mapping.** The readiness mapping above indicates where artifacts support ISO/IEC 42001 themes. It is not a promise of certification, audit outcome or regulatory outcome.

**Incumbent frameworks.** The program is designed to integrate with the existing management systems rather than build parallel structures. Integration points are as follows:

* **Internal audit finding (June 2026):** Week 2. The inventory responds to this finding.
* **ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS:** `Unknown`.
* **ISO 9001 quality management system:** `Unknown`.

The questions to confirm at intake are:

* Which risk registers, document control procedures, management review records and nonconformity processes exist within the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and the ISO 9001 quality management system?
* Where should AI artifacts attach to those registers, procedures and records?

**Second governed workflow.** The minimum viable AIMS requires at least two governed AI workflows in production use by Week 12. The chatbot is deployed. Visual inspection is in pilot, with a stated production target of Q2 2027. A program starting after the decision expected by 15 December 2026 would close no earlier than March 2027. Two items are therefore to confirm at intake:

* Whether visual inspection can enter governed production use within the program window, subject to works council consultation.
* Which other AI uses in production use the inventory may surface as the second workflow.

This is the most important scope decision for Week 1.

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

## 5. Client Team Commitment

The table below gives estimated hours per person per week. These are estimates, not actuals, and will be confirmed at intake. Each person's time covers the workshop, coaching and asynchronous work. Steering weeks add an estimated 1.5 hours per steering attendee.

| Role | Weeks 1 to 5 (estimate) | Weeks 6 to 8 (estimate) | Weeks 9 to 12 (estimate) |
|---|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | 4 | 5 | 3 |
| CISO | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| Head of Quality | 4 | 5 | 5 |
| Head of Data | 5 | 4 | 4 |
| German plant manager | 3 | 3 | 5 |
| Internal auditor (each of two) | 3 | 3 | 4 |

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at three points:

* **Week 1:** mobilization, scope and selection of the second governed workflow.
* **Week 6:** mid-point status, policy adoption route and scope decisions.
* **Week 12:** attestation against the six-element definition and the 12-month operating plan.

Steering attendees are to confirm at intake. Board-level reporting can draw on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 7. Logistics and Price

**Sessions.** All sessions are virtual. The operating jurisdictions span the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, but where build team members are based is `Unknown`. Session times will be set at intake.

**Data handling.** The program workspace is designed so that no customer data is required. Two questions are to confirm at intake:

* Whether the chatbot processes customer data, and where.
* Where program artifacts will be stored, so the EU constraint is respected.

**Price.** The program fee is US$60,000 for the twelve-week Guided AI GRC Build. Payment terms are to confirm at intake. Contract terms: confirm with external counsel.

## 8. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. We propose a short intake session beforehand to confirm the open questions:

* Fiscal year timing.
* Selection of the second governed workflow.
* Integration points with the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and the ISO 9001 quality management system.
* The approach to internal audit independence.
* Whether the build touches production staff, and the sequencing of works council consultation (confirm with external counsel).
* Chatbot data flows.
* Steering attendees.

Week 1 can then be scheduled.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
